finding.claim: wipe() calls requireRole(u, "OWNER") but discards the boolean return value. requireRole only returns true or false and never throws, so the authorization check has no effect. Any authenticated user can wipe any tenant. The sibling export() uses checkRole, which does throw, so the bug is specific to wipe().
finding.source: Any authenticated user without the OWNER role calls POST /tenants/{t}/wipe. The tenant path parameter is attacker-chosen.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27, a destructive wipe of tenant data.

trace.note: requireRole(u, "OWNER") is called as a statement. Its result is ignored and nothing throws.
requireRole returns u.roles().contains(role). Its javadoc says 'Does not throw'.

finding.guards_checked: Checked the whole file. No other role check, exception, or if-guard exists in wipe(). The only guard is the ignored requireRole result. checkRole (line 18), which would throw, is used only in export(). The repo contains no framework annotations, filters, or interceptors that could enforce authorization upstream. Only src/Admin.java exists, so an upstream gateway check cannot be ruled out, but none is visible.

verdict.guard_found: requireRole(u, "OWNER") at src/Admin.java:26 is the only guard. It returns a boolean and never throws (lines 13-16), and wipe() discards the result. checkRole (lines 18-22) throws, but only export() calls it. No upstream filter or annotation exists in the repo.
verdict.reason: src/Admin.java:26 calls requireRole, which only returns a boolean (lines 14-15), as a bare statement, so repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27 runs for any authenticated user, unlike export() at line 32, which uses the throwing checkRole.

finding.claim: Role checks are global and not scoped to the target tenant. A user holding OWNER, for example of their own tenant, passes checkRole and can export or wipe any other tenant by changing the {t} path parameter. This is a cross-tenant IDOR and broken object-level authorization. Plausibility depends on how roles are assigned, which is not visible in this repo.
finding.source: An authenticated user with OWNER (or, via AUTH-1, any user) supplies an arbitrary tenant ID in POST /tenants/{t}/export or /wipe.
finding.sink: repo.export(tenant) at src/Admin.java:33, which exports another tenant's data. repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27 is the equivalent for wipe.

trace.note: checkRole(u, "OWNER") tests only the user's global role set. The tenant argument is not used.
User record has only name and roles. It has no tenant membership field.
repo.export(tenant) runs with the attacker-supplied tenant.

finding.guards_checked: Looked for any comparison between the user and the tenant, such as membership, tenant-scoped roles, or a repo-level ownership check. None exists in this file. The Repo interface is unimplemented here, so a check inside the implementation cannot be ruled out.

verdict.guard_found: checkRole at src/Admin.java:18-22 throws SecurityException unless the user has a global OWNER role, and export calls it at line 32. No tenant-scoped check exists in this file. The Repo implementation is not present.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (checkRole at src/Admin.java:32 ignores `tenant`, and the User record at line 4 has no tenant field), but whether OWNER is a per-tenant role or an intended global/system role depends on role assignment and the Repo implementation, neither of which is in this repo.
